nodes.label: Learning Mechanics: A Scientific Theory of Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Proposes learning mechanics as physics-like theory of neural network training; emphasizes dynamics, coarse aggregate statistics, and falsifiable quantitative predictions

nodes.label: Analytically Solvable Settings in Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Deep linear networks, kernel methods, multi-index models provide intuition; linearization in data and parameters enables exact solutions

nodes.label: Deep Linear Networks
nodes.rationale: Nonlinear in parameters but linear in data; exhibit saddle-point landscapes, phase transitions, edge-of-stability oscillations, and initialization-dependent biases

nodes.label: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK)
nodes.rationale: Describes linearized networks through fixed feature map; enables kernel ridge regression analysis and prediction of generalization error

nodes.label: Infinite Width Limit and Lazy/Rich Dichotomy
nodes.rationale: Initialization scale determines lazy (linearized, no feature learning) vs. rich (feature learning) regimes; mean-field behavior simplifies analysis

nodes.label: Lazy/Kernel/Linearized Regime
nodes.rationale: Weights and representations change negligibly; training dynamics linear in parameters; analytically tractable but lacks feature learning

nodes.label: Rich/Active/Feature-Learning Regime
nodes.rationale: Hidden features adapt to data structure; neurons specialize; exhibits greedy low-rank bias; requires downscaling final-layer weights

nodes.label: Infinite Depth Limit
nodes.rationale: Downscaling per-layer contributions yields smooth residual stream or stochastic dynamics; different limits lead to qualitatively different solutions

nodes.label: Discretization Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Practical neural networks understood as noisy finite approximations to infinite-size models; finite-size corrections worsen performance while saving costs

nodes.label: Neural Scaling Laws
nodes.rationale: Test loss follows predictable power laws in compute, dataset size, and parameter count; exponents remain unexplained but suggest underlying simplicity

nodes.label: Edge of Stability
nodes.rationale: Loss surface sharpness increases then plateaus near 2/η; maximum stable sharpness in convex optimization; decomposable into smooth gradient flow plus oscillations

nodes.label: Neural Collapse
nodes.rationale: Final-layer representations cluster by class around class means forming regular simplex; natural energy-minimizing configuration with cross-entropy loss and weight decay

nodes.label: Neural Feature Ansatz
nodes.rationale: First-layer weight Gram matrix aligns with average gradient outer product; heuristic rule making accurate predictions for weight eigenvectors

nodes.label: Gradient Flow Conservation Laws
nodes.rationale: Difference between covariance and Gram matrices of consecutive layers conserved under gradient flow; follows from Noether principle and continuous symmetries

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Disentanglement
nodes.rationale: Techniques like μP and width-scaling separate hyperparameter effects from core dynamics; enables simpler effective systems and transfer across scales

nodes.label: Universal Phenomena in Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Common inductive biases and representations across models; analogous to critical phenomena and renormalization group flow in physics

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Complementary to learning mechanics; aims to be biology of deep learning while learning mechanics aspires to be its physics

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Disentanglement and Understanding
nodes.rationale: Hyperparameters can be systematically analyzed and understood through theory, enabling transfer across model sizes and configurations.

nodes.label: Linear Scaling Rule
nodes.rationale: Simultaneous rescaling of learning rate and batch size preserves SGD trajectory; enables hyperparameter transfer across batch sizes.

nodes.label: SGD as Discretization of Stochastic Differential Equation
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework that explains the linear scaling rule and predicts optimizer behavior through continuous-time dynamics.

nodes.label: Critical Batch Size
nodes.rationale: Batch size that trades off between serial time and total compute cost; Pareto frontier takes hyperbolic form.

nodes.label: Implicit Regularization of Loss Curvature
nodes.rationale: Optimizer hyperparameters implicitly regularize Hessian; larger learning rates and smaller batch sizes yield stronger regularization.

nodes.label: Tensor Programs Framework
nodes.rationale: Separates scale-independent coefficient from width-dependent factor in hyperparameter scaling; enables systematic analysis of infinite-width limits.

nodes.label: Neural Tangent Parameterization
nodes.rationale: Infinite-width limit where features freeze during training; one of two non-trivial limiting behaviors from Tensor Programs analysis.

nodes.label: Maximal Update Parameterization (μP)
nodes.rationale: Infinite-width limit where features evolve; enables feature learning and hyperparameter transfer across model widths.

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Transfer Across Widths
nodes.rationale: Under μP, optimal hyperparameters remain stable across model widths, enabling tuning on small proxy models and transfer to production models.

nodes.label: Universal Phenomena in Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Diverse architectures, datasets, and training methods exhibit shared behaviors, suggesting simple underlying explanations exist.

nodes.label: Universal Inductive Biases
nodes.rationale: Different architectures (CNNs, Transformers, UNets) achieve similar performance on same tasks, indicating shared implicit biases.

nodes.label: Universal Structure in Data
nodes.rationale: Images, audio, and text share power-law spectral properties, sparsity, multiscale structure, and hierarchical composition across modalities.

nodes.label: Universality in Learned Representations
nodes.rationale: Networks trained on different tasks, datasets, and modalities learn similar internal representations; similarity increases with model size.

nodes.label: Platonic Representation Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Neural activations converge towards a universal representation as model size and performance increase.

nodes.label: Statistical Perspective on Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Classical learning theory frames learning as balancing expressivity, complexity control, and computational efficiency.

nodes.label: Information-Theoretic Perspective
nodes.rationale: Learning as extraction and compression of information from datasets; good generalization results from successful compression.

nodes.label: Physics of Deep Learning Perspective
nodes.rationale: Seeks average-case theories of neural network learning; aligned with development of mechanics of learning.

nodes.label: Neuroscience Perspectives on Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Hypotheses about neural computation (e.g., probabilistic inference) and circuit decomposition inform deep learning theory.

nodes.label: Singular Learning Theory Approach
nodes.rationale: Bayesian framework emphasizing loss landscape geometry and phase transitions; seeks first-principles predictive theories.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Reverse-engineering approach to identify features, circuits, and learned algorithms in trained networks; complements learning mechanics.

nodes.label: Linear Representability Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption in mechanistic interpretability: features correspond to meaningful directions in activation space.

nodes.label: Locality Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: features and circuits are localizable to particular subsets of model components.

nodes.label: Sparsity Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: individual features and circuits are activated on only a small fraction of inputs.

nodes.label: Compositionality Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: complex representations and computations arise from composition of simpler, modular sub-mechanisms.

nodes.label: Induction Heads Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Concrete mechanistic interpretability discovery: circuits that implement in-context learning; target for learning mechanics explanation.

nodes.label: Fourier Features in Algebraic Tasks
nodes.rationale: Mechanistic interpretability finding: networks learn Fourier basis for algebraic tasks; bridges data structure and learned mechanisms.

nodes.label: Developmental Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Research program explaining how mechanisms form during training; bridges mechanistic interpretability and learning mechanics.

nodes.label: Open Direction 1: Solvable Models of Deep Nonlinear Learning
nodes.rationale: Seeks unified framework combining nonlinear parameter dynamics and nonlinear function learning; would illuminate feature learning and architectural innovations.

nodes.label: Open Direction 2: Theory Capturing Natural Data Structure
nodes.rationale: Requires identifying minimal sufficient statistics of data and how they enter predictive theory; essential for bridging theory and practice.

nodes.label: Open Direction 3: Implicit Complexity Minimization
nodes.rationale: Seeks precise characterization of implicit bias towards simple functions; would unify multiple concepts (implicit regularization, simplicity bias, spectral bias).

nodes.label: Open Direction 4: Formal Definition of Features
nodes.rationale: Seeks mathematical grounding for mechanistic interpretability concepts; would formalize and evaluate core assumptions like linear representability and compositionality.

nodes.label: Open Direction 5: Discretization Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Proposes finite networks as discretizations of infinite limits; would unify understanding of width, depth, and learning rate as discretization parameters.

nodes.label: Open Direction 6: Eliminating All Hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Extends hyperparameter disentanglement program; seeks to determine if all hyperparameters can be eliminated through appropriate limits.

nodes.label: Open Direction 7: Predicting Scaling Law Exponents
nodes.rationale: Seeks first-principles prediction of power-law exponents from data, architecture, and optimizer properties; critical test of scaling law theory.

nodes.label: Open Direction 8: Loss Curvature and Generalization
nodes.rationale: Seeks to understand how implicit curvature regularization relates to feature learning and generalization; addresses progressive sharpening phenomenon.

nodes.label: Open Direction 9: Principles of Good Optimizers
nodes.rationale: Seeks fundamental principles explaining optimizer success; would guide design of new optimizers and predict failure modes.

nodes.label: Open Direction 10: Representation Universality Classes
nodes.rationale: Seeks precise characterization of when and how representations converge across training regimes; requires resolving representation similarity metrics.

nodes.label: Learning Mechanics Framework
nodes.rationale: Proposed quantitative, low-level theory of deep learning training dynamics; complements mechanistic interpretability at higher levels of abstraction.

nodes.label: Reynolds Number Analogy
nodes.rationale: Dimensionless parameter predicting fluid flow behavior; analogous to how hyperparameters predict neural network training behavior.

nodes.label: Implicit Inductive Bias
nodes.rationale: Deep learning has implicit bias towards simple, well-generalizing functions; arises from training dynamics and data structure.

nodes.label: Overparameterization
nodes.rationale: High dimensionality of neural networks makes optimization easy despite nonconvexity; enables gradient methods to succeed.

nodes.label: No-Free-Lunch Theorem
nodes.rationale: Generalization on arbitrary data is impossible; deep learning must exploit particular structure present in natural data.

nodes.label: Zipf's Law in Language
nodes.rationale: Word frequencies obey power-law distribution across natural and artificial languages; universal statistical property of text data.

nodes.label: Power-Law Spectral Properties
nodes.rationale: Images and audio signals share power-law spectral properties; universal structure enabling single learning algorithm to handle diverse modalities.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Compositional Structure
nodes.rationale: Both images and text exhibit hierarchical, compositional structure; can be modeled with common frameworks across modalities.

nodes.label: Marr's Levels of Analysis
nodes.rationale: Framework distinguishing physical implementation, algorithmic computation, and computational goals; applied to deep learning study at multiple levels.

nodes.label: Renormalization Group Technique
nodes.rationale: Physics technique formalizing how details wash out at zoomed-out scales; potential analogy for understanding universality in deep learning.

nodes.label: Convergent Evolution Analogy
nodes.rationale: Species solving similar problems find similar solutions; biological analogy for why different architectures learn similar representations.
